Vampires: Gothic, bloodthirsty and fast. Three Vampire lords and Edgar Markov build a curve nobody wants to block, and Blood tokens bridge straight into the Madness cards. For players who want a sleek, menacing aggro deck with real synergy behind it.
Madness & Discard: Discarding a card should cost you something; here it saves you mana. Fiery Temper and friends cast at a discount off looting and Blood tokens, and the hellbent payoffs love your empty hand. For players who enjoy reckless, fast, cost-cutting sequencing.
Zombies: A tribe that simply refuses to stay dead. Gravecrawler and undying bodies recur endlessly while Gisa and Geralf and Grimgrin turn the pile into a dominant board. For players who love grinding, resilient, self-recurring armies.
Spirits: Flying, flash, and never quite there when the removal arrives. Mausoleum Wanderer and Spell Queller pick apart the opponent's turn while evasive Spirits run out the clock. For players who like slippery beatdown backed by counters and tricks.
Werewolves & Wolves: Creatures that punish an opponent for taking a turn off. Transforming werewolves like Huntmaster of the Fells flip into something twice the size, and the payoffs count your growing pack. For players who like beefy threats with a built-in upgrade.
Humans: The deepest creature pool in the cube, all pointed the same direction. Cheap Humans and token engines flood the board while Odric, Lunarch Marshal hands the whole team every keyword at once. For players who love classic go-wide aggro.
Aristocrats / Sacrifice: The deepest sacrifice deck here, where every death is worth something. The Meathook Massacre and Blood Artist drain on each one while free outlets keep the engine fed. For players who love grindy, board-eating value decks.
Spellslinger / Flashback: Every spell gets cast twice, and your creatures are keeping count. Thing in the Ice and Docent of Perfection flip into real threats as you chain instants and sorceries out of the graveyard. For players who love spell-heavy decks and explosive payoff turns.
Tokens & Go-Wide: A board nobody can block profitably, and then an anthem on top of it. Cathars' Crusade and Intangible Virtue make the swarm lethal, and Second Harvest simply doubles it. For players who love flooding the board and overrunning the table.
Self-Mill / Graveyard Value: Your graveyard is the real hand. Splinterfright and The Gitrog Monster grow off the creatures in it, and Hermit Druid plus Laboratory Maniac is a genuine combo kill. For players who like filling the bin and then cashing it in.
Emerge & Eldrazi Ramp: Eat your own creatures to skip several turns of mana. Emerge lets Elder Deep-Fiend and Decimator of the Provinces devour undying fodder and land on the board far ahead of schedule. For players who like a resourceful, sacrifice-fuelled ramp plan.
Blink / ETB Value: Enter-the-battlefield triggers, on repeat. Restoration Angel and Deadeye Navigator reset a board full of ETB creatures until the advantage is simply overwhelming. For players who enjoy value engines and an answer for everything.
Lifegain: Small, steady life gain that quietly becomes a win condition. Voice of the Blessed and Chalice of Life reward the drain and incidental gain your aristocrats cards were producing anyway. For players who like a resilient, grinding game plan.
Voltron / Auras & Equipment: One creature, everything you own, one very short game. Recursive auras like Gryff's Boon dodge the usual card disadvantage and Sigarda, Host of Herons offers a target that removal cannot touch. For players who like all-in single-threat beatdown.
Lands-Matter: Land drops and dead lands both turn into cards. The Gitrog Monster and Wrenn and Seven grind value out of the yard while Cultivator Colossus is the payoff worth ramping toward. For players who love a slow, inevitable grind.
+1/+1 Counters (Training & Coven): A team that trains itself bigger with every combat. Torens makes tokens that pump one another and Hopeful Initiate spends its counters as removal. For players who like a snowballing, synergistic board.
Reanimator: Giants on the battlefield several turns before anyone could cast one. Edgar's Awakening reanimates anything and Through the Breach cheats Griselbrand straight out of your hand. For players who want explosive, game-warping early plays.
Meld: Two cards that fuse into a single monster. Gisela, the Broken Blade and Bruna, the Fading Light combine into something far past curve, and all three meld pairs are here. Since each half is perfectly playable alone, going for the meld is pure upside. For players who enjoy a rewarding two-card payoff.
Exactly Thirteen (Tree of Perdition comb: A combo that wins on an exact number. Tree of Perdition sets the opponent to 13 and Triskaidekaphobia finishes them on your upkeep. A spicy build-around for players who love an unusual alternate win.
